usage: Commonly used for a professional translator who works with spoken or written language, often in offices, schools, media, or public services.
Can refer to someone translating between two languages in a formal, job-related setting; for casual help, people more often just say someone is '幫手譯'.
Usually appears after a number or with classifiers when talking about hiring or counting people, e.g. one translator, two translators.
In everyday speech, this word sounds clear and professional, and it fits better than very general words when you want to show it is a specific occupation.
